title: Developing an Individualized Deep Connectome Framework for ADRD Analysis
text:
This project aims to significantly advance and integrate our powerful methods/tools and apply them to four
Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) and Lewy body dementias (LBD) neuroimaging datasets to discover and identify
individualized connectome-scale differences between AD and LBD, by leveraging the cutting-edge deep learning
techniques.

title: Improving the platelet-mediated immune checkpoint inhibitor delivery for treating triple-negative breast cancer
text:
Immunotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors has achieved great success in treating various types of cancer
clinically, while its treatment efficacy on triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains dismal. In this proposal,
we will develop combination strategies to facilitate the treatment efficacy of platelet-mediated immune checkpoint
inhibitor delivery systems against TNBC. The successful completion of this proposal will develop a suite of new
combination immunotherapy strategies to increase the anti-tumor efficacy against TNBC and provide significant
insights into advancing the current immunotherapeutics for treating other non-immunogenic tumors in the clinic.

title: High throughput identification of bacteriophages and their hosts with single-cell transcriptomics
text:
Bacteriophages (phages) have been repeatedly associated with human disease. Since the majority (>99%) of
these phages have been discovered by culture-independent metagenomics, their bacterial hosts are unknown,
which prevents a mechanistic explanation for how interactions between phages and bacteria influence human
health. This proposal will establish a high throughput phage-host pairing tool based on single-cell prokaryotic
transcriptomics to facilitate the development of culture models to study phage-host interactions.

title: Hematopoietic circRNA-mediated intercellular communication
text:
Liquid biopsies are poised to revolutionize diagnostic procedures by making them more accessible and less
invasive due to the use of biofluids like blood rather than tissue samples. During my PhD I have helped develop
an RNA liquid biopsy platform that the F99 will enable me to lead a validation for in patients diagnosed with lung
adenocarcinoma. As an NIDDK K00 fellow, I will expand the RNA liquid biopsy platform into a hematological
context that will identify extracellular RNA markers of the hematopoietic lineage in- and ex-vivo.

title: Social patterns in sleep deficiencies: The role of stress in the workplace
text:
Black adults experience greater sleep difficulty and shorter duration compared to White adults.
Work-related stress, with its link to sleep deficiencies, may be a critical source of these
disparities. We propose to examine numerous work-related stressors in relation to sleep,
captured through self-reports and biomonitor actigraphy, and clarify biological links, through
continuous ECG and blood pressure monitoring and blood- and saliva-based biomarkers.

title: High-throughput Organoid Platform for Electrophysiology Studies (HOPES)
text:
Organoids provide cutting edge representations of human organs that are an invaluable tool for studying complex
disease and drug interactions with improved in vivo correlation but lack high-throughput automated tools to make
their use for drug screening efficient. We propose to develop a system that can grow and mature cortical brain
organoids, introduce compounds of interest (toxins, drugs, etc), and measure changes in brain activity, in real
time as well as collect effluent for further testing for subsets of organoids for which desired responses are
observed. This platform will enable high-throughput, efficient electrophysiologic interrogation of brain organoids
for drug and toxicity screening and mechanistic studies.

title: Midcareer K24 Award for Mentoring and Patient-Oriented Research
text:
This project will support the candidate’s development as a mentor in patient-oriented substance
use research by providing protected time for advanced training in implementation science,
ecological momentary assessment, adaptive trial design, pain research, mentoring faculty-level
mentees, developing a training for mentors in mentoring through differentness, and supporting a
novel study of non-prescribed stimulant use for neuropathic pain among people living with HIV.

title: Optimization and preclinical evaluation of brain permeant SE-CRISPR to edit ApoE4 after IV infusion in AD models
text:
This proposal is based on our successful CRISPR editing of the apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) gene, the major
genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer’s disease (AD), at the codon for the arginine residue at amino acid-112
to the codon for cysteine found in ApoE3, in ApoE4 transgenic mouse brain, after a single IV infusion of CRISPR
sgRNA+CBE mRNA encapsulated in synthetic exosomes (SEs). SEs are microfluidic reactor-synthesized
deformable lipid nanovesicles the size of natural exosomes developed by our lab as a platform to deliver
macromolecules across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to the CNS. In this proposal, we plan to optimize SE-
CRISPR dosage/dosing schedule, synthesis, and surface modification to enhance editing efficiency E4-5XFAD
mice as monitored by Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), in various brain regions and cell types (neurons,
astrocytes, etc.), as well as measure ApoE3 mRNA and protein expression and the resultant alterations in E4-
specific phenotypes such as memory dysfunction and inflammation, and to test SE-CRISPR editing in E4-KI rat
model to enable translation of this approach to the AD clinic.

title: Defining macrophage defense during Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia
text:
Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia can initiate sepsis, a leading cause of global morbidity that causes immense
socioeconomic burdens as the most expensive hospital treated condition. This research will define host-
pathogen interactions during K. pneumoniae bacteremia, with the goal of identifying pathways that can be
targeted or enhanced by future therapies to aid in the clearance of bacteremia. By defining immunomodulatory
processes of K. pneumoniae bacteremia that could result in novel therapies, this research directly advances the
NIH mission of defining the nature and behavior of living systems to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce
illness and disability.

title: Hippocampal synaptic and circuit mechanisms mediating Dyrk1a functions in social cognition
text:
This proposal seeks to determine how targeting molecular and circuit mechanisms of Dyrk1a
function in the adult brain harbors potential to reverse impact of developmental loss of Dyrk1a
on social cognition in Autism Spectrum Disorders.

title: Comparative Mechanistic and Structural Analysis of Apicomplexan Phosphoethanolamine N-Methyltransferases for Broad-Spectrum Antiparasitic Discovery
text:
Protozoan parasites remain among the most pervasive threats to human and animal health worldwide. In this
project, we will investigate phosphoethanolamine N-methyltransferases (PMTs) from multiple apicomplexan
parasites, essential enzymes required for phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis but absent from mammalian
genomes. By integrating evolutionary, biochemical, biophysical, and structure-guided approaches, we will
comparatively characterize the molecular mechanisms of apicomplexan PMTs and generate foundational
knowledge to support the development of both broad-spectrum and lineage-specific antiparasitic therapeutics.

title: PRAISE (Pressure Relief Assessment Information System): A Paradigm-shifting Mobile Health Platform for Pressure Relief Adherence in Manual Wheelchair Users
text:
TITLE: PRAISE (Pressure Relief Assessment Information System): A Paradigm-shifting
Mobile Health Platform for Pressure Relief Adherence in Manual Wheelchair Users
PROJECT NARRATIVE:
In this project, we will develop a Pressure Relief Assessment Information System (PRAISE),
which aims to enhance adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines among manual wheelchair users
with spinal cord injuries, thereby mitigating the risk of pressure ulcers. Grounded in the
International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, PRAISE will
deliver context-aware feedback and personalized guidance to manual wheelchair users. This
project will not only address a critical healthcare challenge but also promise to provide a
paradigm-shifting mobile health platform that integrates clinical practice guidelines with individual
health, personal, and environmental factors.

title: High-Throughput Functional Annotation of Gene Regulatory Elements and Variants Critical to Complex Cellular Phenotypes
text:
Gene regulatory elements control human development, disease susceptibility and progression,
and almost all complex human traits, however we understand how very few of the millions of
putative regulatory elements in the human genome function. The goal of the Duke IGVF
Characterization Center is to systematically and comprehensively characterize the function of
gene regulatory elements and their variants in diverse biological contexts. We will make our
data, resources, reagents, and analysis tools immediately available to the scientific community.

title: Molecular mechanisms of drug resistance and disease progression in acute myeloid leukemia.
text:
An adverse prognosis subset of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is
characterized by increased expression of a set of homeodomain transcription factors, including HoxA9 and A10.
In preliminary studies, we found such acute myeloid leukemias were also characterized by activation of pathways
involved in the innate immune response. In murine models of Hox-overexpressing AML, we found emergency
granulopoiesis was enhanced and failed to resolve during the innate immune response; associated with
accelerated leukemogenesis and shortened survival. We also found increased expression of proteins involved
in the integrated stress response (ISR) during leukemogenesis in Hox-overexpressing murine models of AML.
These results suggest the ISR may sustain EG and enhance accumulation of mutations leading to AML in the
context of increased Hox expression. Molecular mechanisms involved in this may provide markers of adverse
prognosis in a subset of myeloid malignancies and potential therapeutic targets to delay disease progression.

title: Archaea as a microbial model for developmental mechanoplasticity
text:
Archaea are microbes necessary for human gut health, yet little is known about how they respond under human
physiological conditions. This project aims to study how archaeal cells sense mechanical forces, such as the
ones in body fluids (shear flow) and compression (against animal tissue and by other microbes), and translate
them into biochemical responses. Understanding responses to mechanical stresses will help to connect archaea
to known disease-causing microbes.

title: Validating Mouse Models of Prostatic Hyperplasia
text: SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PROJECT: SUMMARY Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is common, resulting in significant morbidity, billions of dollars in annual medical expenses, and even greater costs to the economy in lost productivity. BPH is characterized by stromal and glandular hyperplasia, occurring focally in the transition zone of the prostate restricting urinary flow. The underlying causes of this focal growth are still unclear. Chronic inflammation is clearly associated with BPH and some have hypothesized a causal link, but data supporting this are limited. No comprehensive description of the immune environment in the mouse prostate currently exists, likely due to the scarcity of prostatic inflammation in background strains. Inadequate characterization of BPH models leaves them subject to scrutiny during the review process, so a direct comparison of mouse models with prostatic inflammation and hyperplasia both to one another and to human tissue is necessary to identify models appropriate to a specific research direction. This project aims to bridge this knowledge gap by utilizing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) to identify the similarities between murine models and human BPH with the hypothesis that specific cell states, with expression profiles that mirror those in human tissues, will be found in individual mouse models indicating those aspects of human disease reflected in the model. The primary objective is to provide a basis to select project-appropriate BPH models through a comprehensive analysis of cellular composition and transcriptomic profiles, supplemented with measures of voiding function and histopathology. Furthermore, these studies will provide an accessible database of cellular, pathological, and voiding function information for each model that can be used as a benchmark and expanded by the benign urologic community. The searchable database will be an invaluable resource for the BPH research community, providing guidance on murine model selection and facilitating molecular and functional queries. Two Specific Aims will be pursued by a multidisciplinary team of three early-stage investigators (ESIs). First, we will complete a comparative cellular and functional characterization of mouse models of prostate hyperplasia. This aim will apply scRNA-seq to individual prostate lobes of six different models of prostatic inflammation and hyperplasia, as well as immune cell profiling for T and B cell receptor sequencing in mouse models and human BPH tissues. Histopathological and voiding function evaluations will also be included. In the second aim, we will develop a reference database and calculate the BPH-indicated functional distance between mouse and reference cellular populations. This aim will provide a bioinformatic comparison of all cells between each model as well as overlay cell types from each model to existing human scRNA-seq data to look for common cell states. Resources to make these data available to the scientific community, as a collection in the CellxGene portal and as an RShiny application, will also be developed in this aim. We anticipate this work will lead to an improved use of current models for BPH research, provide a basis for future R01 applications by each ESI, and lead to future novel pre-clinical studies.

title: Targeted Machine Learning to evaluate and optimize HIV prevention strategies in cluster randomized trials
text:
Cluster randomized trials (CRTs) are essential to evaluating and optimizing strategies deployed at the group-
level (e.g., health clinics and health systems), but are challenging to analyze due to missing data, their smaller
effective sample sizes, and their multilevel data structure. This study will develop, apply, and disseminate new
CRT methods using machine learning to minimize bias due to missing data, maximize statistical power, and
data-adaptively identify multilevel factors contributing to heterogeneity in health outcomes.

title: Technical Mother Machine Core
text:
The Mother Machine Technical Core provides access for each of the subprojects to leading-edge
technology for continuous single cell imaging of populations of thousands to millions of bacteria
per experiment. This capability, which cannot readily be replicated in other labs and is not
commercially available, allows rare cells in an altered physiological state, such as those that
persist despite the presence of otherwise lethal levels of antibiotics, to be examined for
susceptibility to new antibiotics being designed in this P01. It also provides a deep, rich and
precise description of every mutant in a large mixed population, such as mariner transposon
insertions in a Tn-seq mutant pool, along with the ability to recover and further study mutants of
interest, for studies identifying new antibiotic targets.

title: Preserving bone marrow niche integrity and function to rejuvenate aged hematopoietic stem cells
text:
The aging process directly leads to a multitude of diseases that affect nearly all systems of the body, including
blood system. We have discovered a candidate rejuvenation signaling pathway and we intend to test whether
enhancing this signaling axis can restore the functional capacity of an aging blood system. These studies will
lay the foundation for the development of therapeutic strategies to rejuvenate the aged blood stem cell and to
reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with myelosuppression used to treat a wide range of age-related
hematopoietic disorders.

title: Improving Cancer Outcomes In Native American Communities (ICON)
text: ICON will expand authentic tribal-cancer center capacity to improve cancer outcomes for members of Tribal Nations through a coordinated program of research projects addressing three major cancer research priorities as identified by our stakeholders: prevention, screening and cancer care coordination. Career enhancement activities for ICON investigators will be integrated into the research projects, and curricula will focus on the conduct of research in the context of tribal sovereignty. All of this will be accomplished through ICON’s unmatched approaches to community engagement with Tribal Nations.
